title: Big-O Complexity Check
description: Predict the time complexity of common loop shapes.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of a single loop that iterates over every element of an array once?
questions.explanation: One pass over `n` elements means the work grows linearly with `n` — that's `O(n)`.

questions.prompt: A function has a loop inside another loop, both running over the same array. What is its complexity?
questions.explanation: Nested loops over the same input multiply: `n` iterations of the outer loop, each running `n` iterations of the inner loop, gives `O(n^2)`.

questions.prompt: Binary search on a sorted array halves the remaining range on every step. What is its complexity?
questions.explanation: Halving the search range each step means the number of steps grows with `log n`, not `n`.

questions.prompt: A function returns `arr[0]` with no loop and no recursion. What is its complexity?
questions.explanation: No loop and a fixed number of operations means the work does not grow with input size — that's `O(1)`, constant time.

questions.prompt: A function does `3n + 100` operations for an input of size `n`. What is its Big-O complexity?
questions.explanation: Big-O drops constant factors and lower-order terms; `3n + 100` still grows linearly, so it is classified as `O(n)`.

questions.prompt: As `n` doubles, which complexity class sees its operation count roughly quadruple?
questions.explanation: For `O(n^2)`, doubling `n` means `(2n)^2 = 4n^2` — roughly four times the work, unlike `O(n)` which only doubles.
